sections.value:
Security PASS WITH NOTES for #273 at 4000df85fad3260db1d3fbff8791c8f06196a6b1. No security vulnerabilities found in the reviewed delta.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| - | - | - | - | No security vulnerabilities found | - |

Security evidence:
- Return is a delivery trigger, not a new identity grant. Registration retains harness continuity and owner-close refusals (crates/daemon/src/registration.rs:1087-1107); resumption and spawn binding are distinguished from plain renew (1275-1291), and the hook runs after persistence and native receiver attestation (1540-1571,1643-1652). Peer keys remain unable to register or revive through the closed route allowlist (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:470-492).
- Binder admission is unchanged: Claude uses the matching folder/pane session record and observed process start (crates/daemon/src/claude_bind.rs:101-179); Codex checks the spawned child, wrapper parent, exact pane, held thread, saved conversation and process start (crates/daemon/src/codex_bind.rs:270-335).
- The returned seat is passed to the existing drain for its own open holdings; legacy prime holdings are excluded (crates/daemon/src/delivery/role_send.rs:1179-1238). The atomic claim still requires queued state, a live exact seat and an open assignment for the request's project/role/instance (crates/store/src/role_requests.rs:855-903). No authority is taken from the hook's old snapshot.
- Repair commands are advice, not automatically executed. Printable seat/instance guards and per-argument shell_word quoting remain in place (crates/daemon/src/community/picture.rs:93-103,543-602; crates/core/src/directory.rs:31-41). No new secret, machine-local home path or dependency change was identified in the delta.

Proof: just pr-freeze 273 passed twice at this full head. Exact-head CI run 44632177534 passed, including Node 22/24, native contracts, Rust fmt/clippy and 2,595 Rust tests (6 skipped). Successful Rust job 135941400860 uploaded JUnit artifact 14580864261; both named return-hook regressions were independently verified present and passing in that artifact. The security agent also passed an exact-source SQL probe in in-memory SQLite covering wrong seat/project/role/instance, tombstoned/released holders, already-claimed states and queue isolation. That probe is not a Rust or live concurrency test.

Known limits: C33 trusts same-user processes; this verdict does not assert per-seat process authentication. No local builds, mutation runs or live lifecycle probes were performed. Local harness boot reported ready:false because review-worktree dependencies are absent; full harness checks were not run because this is a read-only review and live sensors may mutate shared state. Author mutation results are not claimed as independent security proof. No new loop, timer or launch site is added; the new work is event-triggered holdings/queue reads and existing delivery.

Harness feedback: a read-only review gate combining exact-head CI and successful-job JUnit receipts would avoid dependency-restoration advice and shared-state sensors in detached reviews.
